title: Add invocation fidelity fence and cost-tilt visualizer
author: Priya Mehta
release_notes: Add adaptive fidelity fence sampler to reduce noisy log volume, and a Cost Tilt visualizer dashboard to surface skewed cost distributions across routes and models.
body:
Summary: Introduces two coordinated observability features: (1) an 'invocation fidelity fence' — a lightweight rule-based sampler that gates high-fidelity logs and full-span captures based on a composite score (token-cost, phase-latency anomaly, and recent error density) to reduce storage and processing costs while preserving interesting signals; and (2) a new Grafana dashboard 'Cost Tilt Visualizer' that shows per-route/model tilt (skew) in token-cost vs latency and highlights candidates for batching or model-quantization tuning. Motivation: We have increasing log volume and downstream index costs from capturing full traces for many low-value invocations. Existing sampling is mostly random or cost-only which misses subtle high-latency, low-cost tails and high-cost silent failures. The fidelity fence aims to be cheap to evaluate at the edge, adaptive to recent anomaly signals, and transparent to SREs via metrics. The dashboard fills an ops gap — product teams need to quickly identify routes where cost is concentrated in narrow user cohorts or specific prompt shapes (tilt), so they can prioritize batching, cache rules, or model variant routing. Design: - Fidelity fence: a short-circuit policy evaluated at request admission with inputs: token_estimate, route_id, model_variant, rolling 5m anomaly_score (from runtime detector), recent error_rate_1h, and tenant_tier. The policy computes a composite score S = w1*normalized_token + w2*anomaly_score + w3*error_rate and compares to a tiered threshold (config per base_branch/release channel). When S >= threshold, invocation is marked for full fidelity: full-span, full request/response body capture (scrubbed), and enriched log context. Otherwise, invocation gets compact telemetry (metric-only + sampled span id). The implementation is conservative by default (low w1, higher weight on anomaly_score) and is opt-out via a per-tenant flag. - Cost Tilt Visualizer: a Grafana dashboard with three coordinated views: (A) tilt scatter: per-route/model points where x=median latency, y=median per-invocation token-cost, point size=invocations, color=slope of cost vs latency; (B) cohort drilldown heatmap: prompt-shape buckets x sequence-length, y token-cost quantile; (C) timeline sparklines per-route of tilt-score and fidelity-sampled fraction. Also includes a small synthetic replay panel to run query-band replays on a sample. Implementation details: - Edge policy: implemented in observability-sidecar (edge capture hook). Added a small policy engine module (fidelity_fence.py) with a deterministic scoring function, unit tests, and feature flags. - Telemetry: new metrics emitted: fidelity_fence_eval_total, fidelity_fence_allowed_total, fidelity_fence_blocked_total, fidelity_fence_score_histogram (labels: route, model, tenant_tier). - Traces: When a request is marked full-fidelity we attach tag fidelity=high and add enrichment_key referencing the anomaly window. - Dashboard: added JSON dashboard file under dashboards/cost-tilt-visualizer.json with templating vars for env and model families. - Config: new default policy config in observability-pack/configs/fidelity-defaults.yaml; tenant-level override via tenant-config service supported. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests added for policy thresholds and score normalization. - e2e synthetic replay against staging with 10k synthetic invocations showing 63% reduction in full-trace volume while retaining 91% of anomaly captures. - Canary rollout: started on staging tenants -> canary tenants -> all non-enterprise tenants over a 2-week window. Rollback path: feature flag to disable fence globally; metric alarms on fidelity_fence_allowed_total drop trigger automatic disable. Observability and alerts: - New alerts: fidelity-fence-sampling-drop (if allowed fraction drops > 20% unexpectedly), fidelity-fence-error-rate-increase (if per-tenant error rate rises by >15% after fence enablement). - Dashboard includes an 'impact estimator' panel that estimates monthly storage delta given current allowed fraction. Commits (high-level): ["fidelity: add policy engine and unit tests", "telemetry: emit fidelity_fence metrics and tags", "dashboards: add cost-tilt visualizer + template vars", "configs: default fidelity fence policy and tenant override plumbing", "docs: runbook and rollout notes"] Changed files (high-level): ["observability-sidecar/fidelity_fence.py", "observability-sidecar/tests/test_fidelity_fence.py", "telemetry/metrics_registry.py (adds metrics)", "dashboards/cost-tilt-visualizer.json", "configs/fidelity-defaults.yaml", "docs/observability/fidelity-runbook.md", "deploy/featureflags/fidelity_fence.yaml"] Review conversation (summary): - Aditi Rao (reviewer): "Like the direction. Two asks: add CI unit test for normalization edge-case (zero-variance token estimates) and add a short privacy note in the runbook about scrub patterns." - Author (Priya): "Added unit test and clarified scrub rules in runbook (redaction of PII, maintain compatibility with tenant scrubbing policies)." - Marcus Lee: "Can we reduce weight on token_estimate to avoid biasing toward long prompts? Also request a small perf benchmark showing policy eval latency." - Priya: "Lowered w1 default from 0.6 to 0.2, added a microbench (avg eval time 180ns; p99 520ns) to the PR description and test harness." - Sofia Turner: "Dashboard looks good; consider adding a per-model family aggregator to help sales/CS." - Priya: "Added model_family aggregation and enabled templating." CI: - Unit: pass - Lint: pass (fixed a minor flake8 complaint) - Integration: pass (staging harness) - Load smoke: pass (canary load tests within acceptable bounds) Metrics observed in staging: - Full-trace capture volume: down ~61% - Anomaly recall (sampled): 91% retained - Edge policy eval latency: mean 0.18us, p99 0.52us - Grafana dashboard: tilt scores computed via a 5m aggregation job; query cost is within budget Rollout notes: - Default policy applied to non-enterprise tenants after merge; enterprise tenants remain opt-in until product approval. - Feature flags and tenant overrides available in tenant-config API. - Runbook contains steps to disable fence and to force full-fidelity for a tenant for diagnostic reasons Known limitations and future work: - Current scoring is rule-based; next step is a lightweight ML model to predict signal value per invocation. - Prompt-shape bucketing is coarse; once we deploy more prompt fingerprinting we will refine cohorting. - Cost-tilt visualizer relies on periodic aggregations; adding a streaming tilt estimator is planned. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. All changes guarded behind feature flags and tenant opt-in for enterprise. Related: ENG-7421 (linked linear): ties into the storage cost reduction OKR. Related PRs and references: observability-pack/pr-272222 (privacy-safe summarizers), redwood/pr-118903 (adaptive alert smoothing). Merge: squash merge performed by Aditi Rao. Post-merge actions: - Tag dashboards for release pipeline - Schedule a follow-up in 2 weeks to review impact metrics and adjust thresholds - Notify solutions engineering and platform docs to prepare customer-facing notes
